caption:
Two hours in Shinjuku, Tokyo, before dinner? Garden first, then the city view 🍁

🥇 Shinjuku Gyoen, if your two hours start early
• In autumn the maples in the Japanese Garden turn red, and the Formal Garden has its rows of plane trees. Both are close to the Shinjuku Gate.
• We suggest staying at the Shinjuku Gate end rather than crossing the whole garden, so you are never rushing to leave.
• In winter the gates close early in the afternoon, so the garden is for an early start on a dry day.

🥈 The free Tokyo Metropolitan Government observatory, for later
• It's free and 202 m up, and it stays open into the evening, so it works when the garden has closed.
• Go near sunset for the light and stay for the city lights. Allow about an hour with the walk and the lift queue.
• After dark, a free light projection plays on the building's outside wall, so you can watch it on your way to dinner.

💡 Raining? Stay on the east side around Shinjuku-sanchome, where Kinokuniya's main bookstore connects straight to the subway, so you can browse until dinner without an umbrella.

Between Golden Gai's back lanes and Yasukuni-dori, red gates lead into a quiet shrine where entertainers have long prayed for success ⛩️ DM us GARDEN and we'll send you the way in.
